behavior: `Combobox.Input` in `Combobox.Chips` moves the focus to a chip only when the value is an array. With a value that is not an array, the input keeps the focus and the default action of the arrow key. That key is ArrowLeft in LTR and ArrowRight in RTL. The `null` value of a combobox with no `multiple` prop is such a value. Base UI reads `selectedValue.length` of each value. It throws a `TypeError` for a `null` value. For a string value that is not empty, it prevents the default action of the key at the start of the input. `Combobox.Chip` removes its value for Backspace and Delete only when the value is an array. `Combobox.ChipRemove` removes the value for a press only when the value is an array. With each other value, the part ignores the event. The value does not change, and the part does not prevent the default action or stop the event. In Base UI, the chip reads `selectedValue.length` and throws a `TypeError` for a `null` value. For a string value, it stops the event and throws a `TypeError` at `selectedValue.filter`. The remove button reads `selectedValue[index]` and throws a `TypeError` for a `null` value. For a string value, it throws a `TypeError` at `selectedValue.filter`.
